clue.text: Agrarian regularly in profit

indicators.note: regularly means take every other letter of the word Agrarian, here the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: A farming business turns out to be making money.
explanation.definitionFit: A profit is an advantage or increase earned, which is a synonym of the answer as a noun.

clue.text: Painter friend admits toughness

indicators.note: admits means the word for friend lets the other piece in, holding it inside

parts.note: a mate is a friend
grit is toughness of character

explanation.surface: An artist's companion confesses to having a hard streak.
explanation.definitionFit: René Magritte was the Belgian surrealist artist famous for the bowler-hatted man and the pipe picture.

clue.text: Stunned seeing silver has tarnished (just starting)

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: just starting means only the opening letter of the word tarnished is used

explanation.surface: Someone is horrified to find their silverware has gone dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean shocked and dismayed, struck with amazement or horror: a close synonym.

clue.text: Blemish Church rarely encountered

parts.note: a scar is a blemish on the skin
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A stain on a church that is seldom seen.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seldom met with is in short supply or uncommon, a synonym phrase.

clue.text: Dry hill area

parts.note: sec is the French-derived wine term for dry
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A description of an arid upland region.
explanation.definitionFit: A zone or district of a larger whole, so a synonym for area.

clue.text: Jack abandons outing for Sally maybe

indicators.note: abandons means the letter for Jack leaves the word for outing

parts.note: a jaunt is a short pleasure trip, an outing
J is the card abbreviation for jack

explanation.surface: A man called Jack cancels a trip with a woman called Sally.
explanation.walkthrough: Aunt Sally is a British fairground game of throwing sticks at a figure, and by extension a target of criticism, so Sally is a possible companion word.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairground figure called Aunt Sally makes the female relative a word that can precede Sally.

clue.text: Fuel — one cleaning firm overlooks a litre

indicators.note: in a down entry, overlooks puts the first pieces above the rest

parts.note: a char or charwoman is a cleaner
Co is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A cleaning company ignores a small spill of fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Burnt wood residue used for barbecues and heating is a classic solid fuel.

clue.text: Speech from husband leading to quarrel about article

indicators.note: leading to means the first piece comes before the rest
about means the word for quarrel goes round the article

parts.note: to argue is to quarrel
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A husband's lecture sparks a row about some newspaper piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' looks like a newspaper piece, but here it is the grammatical article.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, forceful, ranting address is a kind of speech.

clue.text: Cloth container very big? Not entirely

parts.note: a can is a container

indicators.note: not entirely means the word for very big loses its final letter

parts.note: vast means very big

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a bag of material is huge, and decides it is not quite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' drops the T of VAST, leaving VAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy woven material used for sails, tents and painting, a type of cloth.

clue.text: Turn made in new way not imagined

indicators.note: in new way means the letters of turn made are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A twist done differently that no one had pictured.
explanation.definitionFit: Something never dreamed of is beyond what anyone pictured, a synonym phrase.

clue.text: Dad's time finished

parts.note: Pa is dad, so Pa's is dad's

explanation.surface: Father's era has come to an end.
explanation.definitionFit: Something over and done with lies behind us, which is a synonym of finished.

clue.text: Food industry feature from Rabat to Iran

indicators.note: the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters sit inside these words, running across the word breaks

explanation.surface: Something characteristic of the food trade stretching from Morocco to Iran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' signals the letters are taken out of the phrase Rabat to Iran.
explanation.definitionFit: A slaughterhouse is part of the meat-supply chain, so a feature of the food business; a slightly grim, oblique description.

clue.text: Fighter moved fast before road rebuilt

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the next

parts.note: tore means rushed, moved fast

indicators.note: rebuilt means the letters of road are put back together differently

explanation.surface: A combatant hurried ahead of a reconstructed road.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullfighter, especially one on horseback, is a fighter in the ring.

clue.text: It's painful at end of splurge to be in debt

parts.note: ow is the exclamation said when something hurts

indicators.note: end of means take only the final letter of the word splurge

explanation.surface: After a spending spree the pain of debt arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: To be obliged to repay money borrowed is to be in debt.

clue.text: Animal alas ain't reformed

indicators.note: reformed means the letters of alas ain't are formed again in another order

explanation.surface: A lament that some creature has not changed its ways.
explanation.definitionFit: This German shepherd dog breed is an example of an animal.

clue.text: US city to sell leading lady aromatic plant

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
to vend is to sell
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen, the country's leading lady

explanation.surface: A star actress travels to an American city to promote a fragrant herb.
explanation.definitionFit: A scented shrub with purple flowers, an example of an aromatic plant.

clue.text: Arrange payment for fish — fed up at first

indicators.note: at first puts that piece ahead of the next
in a down entry, up means the word fed is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: Someone pays for fish because they are fed up with something else.
explanation.definitionFit: To cover or meet the cost of something is to settle the bill for it.

clue.text: In charge of Twickenham sport, heads for London investigating new guidelines

parts.note: RU is rugby union, played at Twickenham, England's national rugby stadium in south-west London

indicators.note: heads for means take the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A rugby official in London looks into fresh rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Being the one who governs or presides means holding authority, so the adjective fits.

clue.text: Just the one fish?

definitions.meaning: only, single, the one and only
a flatfish such as the Dover variety

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a single fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means only or single, and is also the name of a flatfish.

clue.text: Singer of inferior quality, it's said

indicators.note: it's said means the word is heard spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: base means low or of poor quality

explanation.surface: A vocalist who is apparently not very good.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest male voice, and by extension the man who sings it, is a type of singer.

clue.text: Film (U) let out when game's over

indicators.note: out means the letters of film, U and let are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A U-rated film is released once the match has finished.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British cinema rating for films suitable for all ages, which makes the bracket look like a film classification.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the referee's final whistle in football: the moment the match ends.

clue.text: Spy revealed by birthmark?

definitions.meaning: a double agent planted inside an organisation
a small dark spot on the skin

explanation.surface: An agent is unmasked by a mark on the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a planted secret agent and a dark skin blemish.

clue.text: Fabric used in Umbria home on return

indicators.note: on return says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some cloth used in a house in an Italian region on coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the letters sit inside Umbria home.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloth woven from Angora goat hair is a type of fabric, here one that has been used.

clue.text: Girl meets upper-class supporter at recurring intervals

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
U is the label for upper-class usage
an ally is a supporter

explanation.surface: A young woman meets a posh backer from time to time.
explanation.definitionFit: Happening once every year means recurring at regular intervals, a specific example.

clue.text: Cook crossing old street lacking enthusiasm

indicators.note: crossing means the cooking word straddles the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: to fry is to cook

explanation.surface: A chef crosses an old road without much enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold, unfriendly reception shows no warmth or eagerness.
